Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 108, verse 1:

(p-686) Surat al-Kawthar (Sura of Abundance)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar.﴾ It is on the pattern "fawʿal" (fawʿal, a noun form) from "al-kathrah" (abundance), and it means one who is exceedingly abundant. It is said: it is a river in Paradise, sweeter than honey, whiter than milk, colder than snow, softer than butter, its banks are of chrysolite (zabarjad), and its vessels are of silver. And from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father: "It is abundant good." It was said to him: "Indeed, some people say it is a river in Paradise." He said: "It is part of the abundant good."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 108, verse 2:

﴿So pray to your Lord﴾: worship your Lord, who has honored you by His gift, ennobled you, and protected you from the favors of creation, defying your people who worship other than Allah.

﴿And sacrifice﴾: for His sake and in His name, when you slaughter, opposing the idol-worshippers in their sacrificing for them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 108, verse 3:

﴿Indeed, your enemy﴾: indeed, whoever hates you among your people, by opposing them.

﴿He is the one cut off﴾: the one cut off from every good. It is not you, because every person born until the Day of Resurrection from among the believers is your offspring and your descendants, and your remembrance is raised high on the pulpits and on the tongue of every scholar and every remembrer until the end of time. He begins with the remembrance of Allah and follows it with your remembrance. And you have in the Hereafter what cannot be encompassed by description. So one like you is not called "abtar" (cut off); rather, the one cut off is your enemy, forgotten in this world and the Hereafter. It is said: it was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il, who called him "al-abtar." And "al-abtar" is the one who has no offspring. The phrase "huwa" is a separator (fasl, a pronoun of separation), and the predicate of "inna" is "al-abtar."
